title: Putting It into Practice
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/0/bo: Support and resistance on the **higher timeframe** (daily, weekly) usually **matter more**, because more traders see them and bigger orders sit there. A 5-minute level can break easily; a daily resistance, not so much.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/1/ti: Mark levels from the top down
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/1/bo: The routine: first mark the **daily** levels on your chart, then drop to the lower timeframe. When price nears a **daily level** on the 1-hour, look for a **setup** there. Halfway between two levels is usually not a good spot.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/1/ti: On the lower timeframe, a higher-timeframe level is a zone, not an exact line.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/2/pr: On the 1-hour, price has climbed with several bullish candles into daily resistance. Which read is more accurate?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/2/op: A reaction or slowdown here is quite likely
Daily resistance doesn't count on the 1-hour
Price will definitely break through this level
It's the best place to buy big
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/2/ex: Daily resistance is a heavy level, and sellers are more active there. Buying right under it is high risk; better to wait for a reaction or a confirmed breakout.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/3/op: A support that held three times on the weekly
A support that held once on the 5-minute
The close of the last 1-minute candle
A line drawn randomly across the chart
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/3/ex: A higher-timeframe level that's been tested several times is watched by lots of traders and has more orders behind it.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/4/pr: The blue line is daily support. Tap the 1-hour candle that tested this support and bounced.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/4/ex: This candle's lower wick reached 1.0800 and it closed higher. Buyers stepped in at the daily level, and price rose afterwards.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/5/ti: How much room to the next level?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/5/bo: The gap between two higher-timeframe levels is price's **room to move**. If the next level is very close, your target is small and your **risk-to-reward** gets bad. Before you enter, check how much room there is to the **next higher-timeframe level**.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/6/st: Higher-timeframe levels lose their value when you look at them on a lower timeframe.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/6/ex: A daily level is just as important on the 1-hour; it simply shows up as a wider zone instead of a thin line.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/7/pr: You bought near 4-hour support at 1.2720 with a stop at 1.2700. Daily resistance sits at 1.2750. What's the risk-to-reward to the daily resistance?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l1/steps/7/ex: Risk is 20 pips and reward is 30 pips: 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5. The nearby daily level caps your profit room; many traders would pass on this trade.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/title: Entry Triggers on the Lower Timeframe
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/0/bo: A **Trigger** is the specific event on the **lower timeframe** that says "now's the time to enter": for example, an **engulfing candle**, a **break of a small trendline** or a **break of the last high (BOS)** on the 15-minute, once price has reached a higher-timeframe level.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/1/bo: Entering on the lower timeframe means your stop goes **below the small setup's low**, not below the whole 4-hour structure. With the same target, your **risk-to-reward** gets much better.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/1/ti: A tighter stop also gets hit sooner; the advantage is only real when your trigger is valid.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/2/pr: Price reached 4-hour support, and on the 15-minute you bought at 1.2718 on a bullish engulfing. Place your stop using lower-timeframe entry logic.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/2/ex: With a 15-minute trigger, the stop goes below this small setup's low: the low is 1.2694, so somewhere like 1.2690 (about 28 pips of risk). Below the whole 4-hour zone (under 1.2680), the risk would be 40 pips or more. Remember, a tighter stop also gets hit sooner.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/3/pr: On the 15-minute, price has reached daily support. What trigger is the last candle?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/3/ex: The last candle's green body fully covers the red body before it. A bullish engulfing on daily support is a common buy trigger.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/4/pr: Price reached 4-hour support, and the 15-minute structure has been bearish. Tap the candle that broke above the **last lower high (LH)**.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/4/ex: This is the first candle that closed above the last LH (1.0829). The 15-minute bearish structure broke (BOS), and that's a buy trigger on 4-hour support.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/5/pr: GBP/USD's 4-hour trend is up and price has reached 4-hour support. On the 15-minute, a small downtrend line just broke with a strong green candle. What do you do?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/5/ex: Three things line up: a 4-hour uptrend, price on 4-hour support, and a 15-minute trendline break. A move up is more likely, and the stop goes below the small setup's low.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/6/bo: Price reaching a higher-timeframe level **isn't a reason to enter on its own**; the level might break. A lower-timeframe trigger shows the reaction has **actually started**. If no trigger shows up and price breaks the level, be glad you stayed out.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/7/pr: Put the steps of a multi-timeframe entry in order.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/7/it: Identify the trend on the daily
Mark the key level on the 4-hour
Wait for price to reach the level
Wait for a trigger on the 15-minute
Enter with a stop beyond the setup's low
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/7/ex: Top down: direction, level, patience, trigger, and finally an entry with a clear stop loss.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/8/st: With a lower-timeframe stop, you can trade a bigger position for the same dollar risk.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/8/ex: Position size = risk amount ÷ stop distance; a smaller distance means a bigger size for the same risk. But a tighter stop also gets hit sooner.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/9/se: The ___ on the lower timeframe tells you when to enter, and the ___ on the higher timeframe tells you where.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l2/steps/9/ex: The higher-timeframe level sets the trading zone, and the lower-timeframe trigger sets the moment to enter.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/0/bo: Timeframes often **don't agree**: the daily is up and the 1-hour is down. That usually means the lower timeframe is **pulling back**. As long as the higher-timeframe structure hasn't broken, **the higher timeframe has the final say**.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/1/bo: When timeframes disagree: 1) **wait** until the lower timeframe lines up with the higher one again (for example, by breaking the previous high); 2) if you trade against the trend, keep it **short and small**; 3) **step aside** completely. For most people, option one is best.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/2/pr: Daily up, 4-hour up, 1-hour down. What's the best read?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/2/op: The 1-hour is probably pulling back; wait for it to turn
The main trend has changed; time to sell big
Forget the higher timeframe and only watch the 1-hour
Ignore all three and trade at random
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/2/ex: The two bigger timeframes are up, so the 1-hour drop is most likely a temporary pullback. A good entry comes when the 1-hour turns up again.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/3/pr: The daily is up. The 1-hour had a bearish pullback and has just broken above its last lower high (LH). What do you do?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/3/ex: Breaking the last LH means the 1-hour pullback is probably over and the lower timeframe is back in line with the daily trend. A continuation up is more likely, with a stop below the last low.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/4/ti: When the higher timeframe is turning
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/4/bo: Sometimes the lower timeframe is right and the higher timeframe is **reversing**. The sign is when the **higher timeframe's own** structure breaks too, like the **last higher low (HL)** breaking on the daily. Until then, the lower timeframe's disagreement is just a **warning**.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/5/pr: On BTC's daily, price has broken below the last higher low (HL). What does this mean?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/5/op: The daily uptrend is in doubt; the buy filter has weakened
Nothing; the daily is still definitely up
It's the best time to buy with high leverage
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/5/ex: An uptrend is defined by higher lows. A close below the last HL means the bullish structure has broken; you should stop buying or be very careful until the picture clears.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/6/st: When the 1-hour moves against the daily, it always means the daily trend is over.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/6/ex: Most of the time it's just a pullback within the bigger trend. A daily trend change is only confirmed when the daily structure itself breaks.
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/7/pa: All timeframes point the same way
A temporary move against the higher-TF trend
A structure break on the higher timeframe
Not trading when the picture is unclear
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/8/pr: Gold is up on the weekly, but price has reached a major weekly resistance. A buy trigger showed up on the 1-hour, but there's only $10 of room to resistance and your stop is $12 away. What do you do?
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/8/op: Pass; the reward is smaller than the risk
Buy with high leverage since the weekly is up
Remove the stop to give it room
Sell, since the 1-hour gave a buy
lessons/multi-timeframe-u2-l3/steps/8/ex: The trend agrees, but weekly resistance is right overhead: $10 of reward against $12 of risk (worse than 1:1). Better to wait for resistance to break or for price to pull back.
